narrative.overview:
Dark, compact surfaces let real scenes, people and creations supply the color. Inter headings, quiet metadata and small pink selection marks keep browsing legible. Controls feel direct; cards frame content without becoming decoration.

This boundary extends the current Social content appearance and Explorer shell. The [lobby design](../explorer/pages/lobby/DESIGN.md) remains the authority for its plaza, live avatar and composition. Its translucent scene overlays are local to that experience. Shared content styling does not redefine the lobby or HUD.
keyCharacteristics: Dark tonal layers with subtle borders.
Compact pink navigation and clear primary actions.
Real scene imagery, stable image space and readable metadata.
Shared primitives with product-owned layouts and behavior.

rules.name: The Stable Selection Rule
rules.body: Controls above map imagery keep an opaque base. Map selection mixes accent into panel color; it must not expose changing map pixels through the selected fill.

rules.name: The Consumer Boundary Rule
rules.body: UI3 owns reusable appearance and components. Consumers own routes, queries, layout composition and product actions. Both `catalyrst/sites` and `catalyrst/social` resolve `@ui/*` through sibling `../ui3/src/*`; keep those sibling paths and share imports instead of copying CSS.

dos: Do reuse shared tokens and primitives before adding consumer styling.
Do keep real scene imagery, complete categories and all calendar days.
Do preserve the lobby composition and live avatar under its own design.
Do show visible focus, honest content states and refresh recovery.
Do label nonlocal calendar times and keep map controls opaque.
donts: Don't copy shared component CSS into Sites or Social.
Don't apply this content boundary as a replacement for the lobby or HUD.
Don't hide categories or days to make a narrow layout fit.
Don't replace missing data with invented activity or decorative imagery.
Don't treat this extension as a completed site-wide migration or CSS target.
